definitions.gloss: to hurt, to injure, to wound

examples.japanese: {傷|きず}つけるつもりはなかった。
examples.english: I didn't mean to hurt you.

notes:
{傷|きず}つける means to hurt, injure, or wound—either physically or emotionally.

TRANSITIVITY:
- {傷|きず}つける (transitive): to hurt, wound
- {傷|きず}つく (intransitive): to get hurt, be wounded

CONJUGATION (ichidan):
- {傷|きず}つけない (negative)
- {傷|きず}つけます (polite)
- {傷|きず}つけた (past)
- {傷|きず}つけて (te-form)
- {傷|きず}つけられる (passive: to be hurt)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {人|ひと}を{傷|きず}つける: to hurt someone
- {心|こころ}を{傷|きず}つける: to hurt someone's feelings
- {体|からだ}を{傷|きず}つける: to injure one's body
- {車|くるま}を{傷|きず}つける: to scratch a car
- {傷|きず}つけるつもりはなかった: I didn't mean to hurt you

WORD FORMATION:
{傷|きず} (wound) + つける (attach/cause) = to cause a wound

RELATED WORDS:
- {傷|きず}: wound, injury, scratch
- {傷|きず}つきやすい: easily hurt, sensitive
- {怪我|けが}をさせる: to injure (cause injury)
